meta.title: Ondra Study Companion
meta.description: Ondra's study companion (L9 extension pool): while someone studies it keeps exactly one thing in order — the rhythm of focus segments and rest segments. It answers two questions only: is this focus segment still alive, and should we take a break. There are exactly two ways to advance it: an external tick(now) and a low-frequency checkpoint(). Nothing in this plugin counts time on its own — no setInterval, no setTimeout, no inferring elapsed time from file timestamps — because a resident timer keeps adding minutes while nobody is watching, and then closing the window for eight hours and coming back reads 'studied eight hours today', when not a single second of those eight hours was spent studying. Time is only ever what the caller hands in, and if the gap between two ticks is too large (15 minutes by default) the segment is judged interrupted and not one second of it is counted; the state file records 'was interrupted' rather than 'completed this segment', because merging the two would credit her with work she did not do. stop() reuses exactly the same gap check as tick(), otherwise closing the app for three hours and then pressing stop reopens the same hole. A break prompt must always be refusable: in the contract declinable is the literal type true and mandatory is the literal type false, so the type system has no branch for 'must', and it never locks the screen, pops a window or interrupts; after a refusal it steps back on a cooldown, and the cooldown is not a punishment but the only thing that makes a refusal mean anything. No assessment, no scoring, no 'study score for today' — once a score exists someone will let the plugin count minutes for them so the score looks good. No note text and no study content are stored: start(subject) receives a subject name and then throws it away, because storing it is storing study content. Crossing midnight clears today's totals but keeps the 'has ever started' flag: clearing it makes the first read of the next day say 'never started', which is false reassurance for someone who studied two hours yesterday. No streak calendar, no consecutive-day counter — that is attendance tracking, and attendance starts lying on day one. No UI; rendering belongs to the app shell. State lives in user/study.json, mode 0600, written atomically via a temp file plus rename, holding timestamps and millisecond counts only. All four upstreams (ondra-clock, ondra-identity, ondra-path-layout, ondra-config-schema) are soft dependencies: without the clock it falls back to the local time zone, without the path service it stays in memory, and both show up in the stored flag and in the log. Degradation must be visible.
